gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-bengali: Styro is retro and crowded, its letters pressed nearly shut. Noto Sans Bengali, with open mouths and capitals barely above the lowercase, loosens things up beside it, a modern counterweight to all that tightness.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-brahmi: Styro is retro and commanding, with letters packed so tight the gaps nearly vanish. Noto Sans Brahmi sets its mean line high and leaves every curve open-ended, so the two feel like a shout and a sigh.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-buginese: Styro makes a loud retro statement with crowded, nearly sealed letters. But Noto Sans Buginese, whose open mouths curve like unjoined chalk arcs, does the quieter work of carrying text.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-cherokee: Letters pressed nearly shut, with barely a gap anywhere, give Styro its retro force. And Noto Sans Cherokee, with a tall band of letters and an e whose terminal gapes wide, keeps reading approachable.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-chorasmian: Loud, crowded, retro: Styro packs its letters until the gaps nearly disappear. Noto Sans Chorasmian, with curves that stop short and a large x-height, makes reading feel open and unhurried.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-coptic: Tightly crowded letters with barely a gap give Styro a retro, commanding look. Noto Sans Coptic lets its dominant middle zone and open s and c carry the reading, clean and contemporary.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-devanagari: Noto Sans Devanagari reads modern and unfussy, with an open-curved g and capitals that melt into lowercase. But Styro presses its letters close, so the move from heading to text feels like stepping into open air.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-duployan: Pressed-tight letters with barely any gaps inside them give Styro a commanding, retro look that announces itself. Noto Sans Duployan, with wide-mouthed a and oversized counters, is the generous opposite.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-gujarati: Letters pressed nearly shut make Styro feel retro and commanding. It earns its keep big and brief, while Noto Sans Gujarati's clean curves, which end before turning inward, handle everything else.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-hebrew: Styro is all retro command, letters pressed tight. That makes it ideal for an entrance, while Noto Sans Hebrew, with a dominant midsection and wide gaps beside the stems, handles the carrying.
